juan_customer: Hi team — embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings is intermittently returning 400 dimension_mismatch and occasionally 500s, plus big tail latency spikes (~2.5–6s) since yesterday. Mostly from eu-west-1. Random requests succeed next to failing ones. Any pointers?

nora_support: Sorry about that, Juan. Can you share a minimal repro (curl or SDK snippet), the model name, and whether you're on Hosted vs Dedicated capacity? Also sticky: are you using dynamic batching with a large max_batch_size?

juan_customer: We're on hosted. Model: text-embedding-3-small. Quick repro (redacted API key):

```bash
curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":["my text","another text"]}'
```

Responses are inconsistent. Error payload looks like: `{\"error\":\"dimension_mismatch: expected 1536 but got 2048 for request id xyz\"}` or sometimes 500 with no body.

matt_eng: @nora_support @juan_customer couple of quick hypotheses: 1) dynamic batching mixing requests for different model variants (e.g., quant vs non-quant) can produce dimension_mismatch if routing allows mixed-model coalescing; 2) clients sending empty strings or binary blobs end up as zero-length vectors and confuse the batcher; 3) retry storms (401/403) can flood the queue and cause big batches + tail latency. What are your batching settings?

juan_customer: We never changed defaults in our SDK — checking config: dynamic_batching: true, max_batch_size: 128, coalescing_window_ms: 12, priority: default. Retries were naive (no jitter), retry_count: 5.

sara_infra: Quick infra checklist: 
- Check batch-assembler logs for mixed model_hash in a single batch.
- Search ingress logs for repeated 4xx auth errors from the same client before spikes.
- Confirm no client is submitting base64 or non-UTF8 strings (we've seen that cause parser fallbacks).

deploy-bot: ingress-log 4271000023 - 401 Unauthorized - api_key=redacted - source=juan-customer-service

juan_customer: Oh — one of our service tokens rotated and expired yesterday. We started seeing 401s and our client retried immediately.

matt_eng: That matches. Retry storms produce a flood of tiny requests that the coalescer will squash into the next outgoing batch. If a large legitimate request arrives at the same time, the batcher pads everything to the largest vector size or model dims, producing heavy memory + compute and long tail latency. Also mixed-model coalescing can silently include different embedding variants if routing isn't pinned.

Suggested immediate mitigations: 
- Rotate/replace the expired token (urgent).
- Add exponential backoff + jitter and lower retry_count on the client.
- Temporarily lower max_batch_size to 32 and reduce coalescing_window_ms to 6 to reduce batch buildup.
- In routing policy, set allow_mixed_model_variants=false or pin model version to avoid mixing quant/non-quant variants.

nora_support: I'll apply a temporary routing override for your customer id to prevent mixed-variant coalescing and blacklist the older key to stop retried 401s hitting the pool. Can you try the client-side changes and report p95/p99?

juan_customer: Applying changes now (rotated key + backoff + set max_batch_size=32 locally). Will run a traffic replay for 15 minutes and report.

olivia_oncall: I'll monitor the embeddings pool (eu-west-1) for queue length, batch sizes, and tail latency while they test.

juan_customer: Update ~10m later: errors disappeared, p95 dropped from ~2.8s to 180ms, p99 back to expected. No dimension_mismatch after pinning model variant and rotating token. Thanks :thumbsup:

nora_support: Great — filing KB with reproduction notes and the temporary routing patch. Follow-up: we'll add a guard in the batcher to refuse mixed-model coalescing unless explicitly allowed and add a metric for consecutive 4xx spikes to auto-throttle client retries.

juan_customer: Thanks everyone — please keep me posted on the KB and the permanent fix.
